bugs.text: If the Boss is shot while the ship is being pulled up, updateCapture just clears player.captured and never resets player.y, so the fighter carries on at whatever height it had reached instead of returning to the bottom row.
Results screen: the hit-miss ratio value prints over the end of the 'HIT-MISS RATIO' label (visible in 4-play-030s.png).
The captured fighter never fires at the player when its Boss dives (spec item missing).

If the player dies on the stage's last enemy (for example by ramming it) with no ships left, beginIntro revives the player (alive=true, respawn=0) before the game-over check runs, so the player gets a free extra life.
The READY and in-play STAGE overlay counters are advanced in render(), so how long those texts show depends on the monitor's refresh rate.
Challenging-stage enemies skip the body collision entirely and fly through the player harmlessly.
The ship is drawn white while being pulled up by the beam; it only turns red once held above the Boss.
The formation keeps swaying while it breathes instead of switching from sway to breathing.
The freed fighter targets player.x-15, but docking keeps the centre at player.x, so the pair jumps 7.5 px on docking; a fighter freed while the player is already dual is silently discarded.
SFX.hit is never used; a non-Boss hit and its kill share one sound.

summary: A tidy, compact, faithful clone. Load is clean, the curved group entries look right, the formation breathes, dives loop and re-enter from the top, and Boss escorts score 400/800/1600 by escorts left. The tractor beam, capture (the play-test caught a real capture: a red fighter held above a hit Boss), rescue, dual fighter with per-half loss, challenging stages with correct bonuses, arcade badge denominations, the results screen and localStorage high score all work through reachable code. Gaps: the captive never fires, plus a handful of small rule and presentation slips (results text overlap, the ship not red while pulled, sway continuing during breathing, a stuck-height edge case when the beaming Boss is shot mid-pull, render-tied overlay timers). The code is split into sections with separate update and render functions but carries noticeable dead code and odd `&& false` / `% 1` conditions. It feels like Galaga.
